traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report covers three PCR instruments (PikoReal - discontinued, 7500 Fast, and QS5) each with its own Table 10/11/12 giving 17 food categories (with sub-protocols/instruments/incubation times), plus multiple 'All products (including PPS)' aggregate rows (A-H) that were excluded as totals. I treated Table 10 (PikoReal PCR Instrument, categories 1-7) as the primary/canonical study since it appears first and is the original certified instrument list; the 7500 Fast and QS5 tables (Tables 11 and 12, categories 1-17, essentially identical data with extension categories 8-17) are extension studies covering additional categories (Milks/dairy, Infant formula, Vegetables, Seafood, Raw beef meats at 9h/24h, Environmental samples, Milk powder/Infant formula/cereals, Cocoa/chocolate NFDM and BPW, Pet food 1-in-6 and 1-in-10, Meat products 375g/25g at 8h/24h, Powdered infant formula, Fresh/processed vegetables and fruit, Animal feed, Primary production samples) and were not extracted in detail per the instruction to record only the primary/canonical study categories. Category 1 'Meat products' in Table 10 has sub-rows a/b/c (Unprocessed, Processed, RTE/RTRH) which were combined into the Total row values reported here, consistent with the row structure of the table. Certificate number formatted as printed on cover page ('UNI 03/07 – 11/13'). No Acceptability Limit or quantitative bias/SD data present since this is a qualitative (detection) method, so the 'quantitative' object is null.
